full_judgment: 4. In the plaint, it has been stated inter alia, that the plaintiff's predecessor Ali Mohammad purchased .76 acre of land with definite boundaries fully described in the registered kabala No. 1171 dated 13.7.26 from Karimon Shah and others who purchased the said .76 acre of land with similar boundaries described in the registered kabala dated 14.12.1921 from Dari Goala, owner of 3 plots i.e. plot No. 77 measuring .62 acre of land, plot No. 59 measuring .63 acre of land and plot No. 58 measuring 11 acre of land. Karimon Shah and his co-purchasers got possession of their purchased land as described in their kabala by boundaries. i.e. northern side of C. S. plot Nos. 77, 59 and 58 and possessed the said land peacefully and uninterruptedly. By purchase All Mohammad also got possession of the same land and peacefully and uninterruptedly possessed. After his death, the plaintiff's had been in peaceful and uninterrupted possession of the entire .76 acre of land out of C. S. plot Nos. 77, 59 and 58. The said land contained the boundaries :-North : Homestead of Asalat; South; land of Damrigoala sold to Moroni's mother; East Road and West: East bank of tank belonging to Karuna Balm. By mistake and inadvertance of the scribe, plot Nos. 58 and 59 were not mentioned in the documents of Karimon Shah and others but only plot No. 77 was mentioned. When Ali Mohammad, predecessor of the plaintiffs. purchased the said .76 acre of land from Karimon Shah and others the same mistake crept into his deed also. Plot No. 59 is adjacent west of plot No. 77 and plot No 58 is adjacent west of plot No. 59. plot No. 57 is Karuna Babu's Pukur is adjacent west of plot No. 58. This will be abundantly clear from the C S. map of the Mouza. In the revisional settlement plaintiffs possession in C. S. plot No. 77 has Len recorded as R.S. plot No. 557 with an area of .36 acre. Petitioner's possession in C. S. plot No. 59 has been recorded in two plots being R. S. plot No. 558 with an area of .21 acre and R. S. plot No. 627 with an acre of .10 acre of land. This .67 acre together with .09 acre of C: S. plot No. 58 constitute .76 decimals of plaintiffs land. It has been further alleged that through undue influence of Dr. A. Gafur, husband of Begum Rabeya Khatun, the said .009 acre of plot No. 58 was not recorded in the name of the plaintiffs but the entire land of dag ho. 58 including plaintiff's .09 acre of land has been wrongly recorded in the revisional settlement record in the name of Begum Rabeya Khatun who has no semblance of any right nor any scrap of paper in support of her alleged title and claim in respect of Plot No. 58 measuring .11 acre of land. Defendant No. 2 Begum Rabeya Khatun wife of Dr. Abdul Cafur purchased 4 kathas of land i.e. 71/2 acre of lard by kabala No. 3992 dated 12.8.1949 from Mehini Mohan Dry Bhowmic who purchased 10 kathas of land from Ali Ahmed who purchased 10 kathas cf land from plot No. 77 and 59 in two lots i.e. front plot No. 77 and 59 and from plot No. 58 and 59 from Muktakeshi Devi alias Moroni's mother who actually purchased .36 acre of land from Damri Goala from plot No. 77 and 59 and 58 though in the kabalas plot No.58 was mistakenly omitted tut in the boundaries given in the kabala covered the dug No. 58 as well. The boundaries of the 4 kathas of lard of kabala No. 3992 dated 12. 8. 1949 of Begun Rabeya Khatun defendant No. 2 from aforesaid Mohini Mohon Bhowmic are as under :-North Homestead of Ali Ahmed, South : P. W. Road, East : Kedar Nath Mukherjee now Felani Bibi and Khas tank. According to the plaintiffs by the said kabala No. 3992 dated 12. 8. 49 the above .1 kathas of and purchased by Begum Rabeya hatun Ire m the extreme south western Fortis n of dag Nos. 58 and 59 with a clear measurement of above 4 kathas. The measure tent of four boundaries which has been shown in the trap attached to thekabala deed are as under:- North boundary line 34'-6", South 28'-7", East boundary line 85'-3" and West boundary line 91'-4". Thereafter, the plaintiff; stated that with re-raid to requisition and acquisition of part of the suit land in L. A. Case No. 11 of 1961-62 and the quantity of land Was taken into possession by the Government, and the amount of compensation have been paid to the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs mentioned about the direction received from the Land Acquisition Collector to take recourse to the Civil Court for declaration of title to C. S. plot No. 59 but the same was cancelled subsequently. The plaintiffs obtained a direction from the Board of Revenue with regard to payment of compensation. Thereafter, the plaintiffs filed an application on 15th June, 1971 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Development) Dacca to acquire the strips of land originally requisitioned and acquired subsequently left from final acquisition, re-demarcate the land and pay compensation thereof according to the order of the Board of Revenue. According to the said direction of the Board of Revenue, the Additional Deputy Commissioner passed the necessary order directing the Special Land. Acquisition officer to re-demarcate the land in order to give effect to the direction but due to some unknown reason the matter is still pending. The plaintiffs assert that they are in peaceful possession of .09 acre of land of plot No. 58 for a period over 12 years but on 31.10.64 the defendant No. 2 with a malafide intention filed case No. 1310a'64 under section 144 Cr. P. C. through her husband Dr. M. A. Gafur in respect thereof and illegally obtained an exparte order of injunction restraining the plaintiffs from entering in to plot No. 58, with the ulterior motive of grabbing the dag No. 58 under the cover of the ex-parte order.
